events.region: Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM; Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1115 AM EDT.

* At 940 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 16 nm
southeast of Buckeye Reef to near Suwannee River, moving southeast
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee River.

events.region: Central Copper Valley; Southern Copper Valley; McCarthy
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 78 to 83.

* WHERE...Central Copper Valley, McCarthy, and Southern Copper
Valley.

* WHEN...From 2 PM this afternoon to 9 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Daytime temperatures across the Copper River
Valley will climb to around 80 degrees through Sunday. The warmest
temperatures will be along the Edgerton Highway and McCarthy Road.
Overnight lows will drop into the lower to mid 40s, allowing for a
brief respite from the very warm temperatures.
